FIX ROUND 634m for story #634, slice A (decision 0083: an adopter's Brokkr lives in one .brokkr/ folder; folder discovery, the defaults that follow from it, and the old-layout refusals), on branch story-634-slice-a, already checked out in this worktree at 6d46af6a.

You are building exactly one OPERATOR RULING, nothing beside it. The issue text at the end is the framing; the slice's own facts follow under HOST FACTS. Decision 0071 (the architectural principles) is ACCEPTED. Build to it.

THE RULING (operator, in chat, 2026-10-14, option 1): ANY symbolic link in or under .forge, and a .forge that is itself a symbolic link, makes the old-layout refusal list NO moves and refuse by name: "move it yourself". This applies at any depth: the ignore file, a journal, a results directory, an entry nested anywhere below.
WHY: the last four review rounds each found a more contrived link spelling that the move list's link resolution got wrong:
- a .forge linked to the root or an ancestor;
- a relative link escaping .forge;
- an absolute link reaching .forge through a `..` detour or a linked ancestor;
- a linked ignore file.
Each fix exposed another spelling. The operator ruled to stop resolving links: one rule, refusal, ends the class. Adopters with links under .forge are rare, and they move their state themselves.

HISTORY OF THE BRANCH (latest first)
- 6d46af6a, 7832ced6, cea25b8f: the fourth landing's (landing-pr-for-story-634-slice-a-0959df12) three implement rounds, all about links:
  - crates/brokkr-cli/src/folder/links.rs (links_stay, stays, enters, escapes, outside, LinkRefusal::{Escaping, InRepository});
  - FolderError::ForgeHoldsRoot;
  - LinkedTracked's index check (tracked::Index { names, itself });
  - their property-table rows.
  The operator stopped that landing under this ruling.
- fff310e0 (the controller's): Sparse, and LinkedTracked's reason.
- Fix round 634k (83251f2d, beb31337, f521529a): MapSource::now's Ambient arm, folder_bundle by Kind, tracked.rs (Uncommitted, TrackedSubmodule, Unwatched), and enum Move with builder_arms.
- Earlier rounds 634b, 634c, 634i and 634j, and the controller's merges of main (latest 54ae5d12, main a0632cb6).
- When you are done, the branch is the above plus ONE new commit of yours. Do not rebase, squash or amend.

BUILD THE RULING, with binding tests and removal controls (plant the shape, see the test fail with the stated text, remove the plant):
1. ONE link rule, as the first thing the move-list builder decides.
   - Walk .forge's entries at every depth by symlink_metadata. Never follow a link, and read the root .forge entry itself the same way.
   - If .forge itself, or ANY entry under it, is a symbolic link, refuse with a single FolderError variant naming the first link found, in sorted walk order. Choose the variant's name; Link { path } is fine. Its text: "{path} is a symbolic link, and Brokkr lists no moves through or for one (decision 0083; the operator's ruling of 2026-10-14); nothing was opened: move the state into .brokkr/state yourself, then run again".
   - An entry or directory the walk cannot read refuses as Unreadable with its path, as today.
   - This runs BEFORE any git question, so a linked .forge never reaches tracked().
2. DELETE what the rule makes unreachable, and no more:
   - links.rs's link resolution (stays, enters, escapes, outside, LinkRefusal and its variants). Keep a walk function if you put the rule there, and keep the file only if it still earns its place;
   - FolderError::ForgeHoldsRoot and FolderError::LinkedTracked;
   - tracked::Index.itself, if nothing reads it;
   - Forge::Link and Move::Unlink, with the "# .forge is a link" comment line and the `rm .forge` arm;
   - the ignore-file arm's link case. A link there now refuses by the one rule; a regular file still gets rm or git rm; anything else still refuses as IgnoreNotAFile.
   Every deleted variant's pinned text and test goes too. A test whose shape is now refused by the one rule becomes a row asserting the one refusal.
   - KEEP everything not about links: Sparse, Uncommitted, TrackedSubmodule, Unwatched, Untracked, NotUtf8, ControlCharacter, IgnoreNotAFile, the HalfMoved/Root/StateOnly refusals, MapSource::now, folder_bundle, and the places.rs layout judgement.
   - Old-layout DETECTION is unchanged. 0083 ruling 4 still judges a linked .forge an old layout, by lstat: only the move LIST refuses.
3. The property test brokkr_folder::the_listed_moves_empty_every_forge keeps executing every arm of enum Move, and builder_arms still reads enum Move off src/folder.rs. Its link rows become refusal rows for the one rule, at four depths:
   - .forge itself a link;
   - .forge/.gitignore a link;
   - .forge/forge.db a link;
   - a link two directories down (.forge/results/run/out -> elsewhere).
   Each asserts the exact text and that NO file moved and nothing was created.
   Removal control: skip the walk for nested entries; the nested row then prints a list.
4. Update every doc comment and the decision text this slice wrote that described the link handling, so nothing claims links are moved or resolved. Decision 0083's text is the operator's: do NOT edit it. Name in your notes the sentence of 0083 ruling 4 that this ruling narrows, for the operator's later addendum.

THE ISSUE (#634), verbatim:

## Why

`brokkr init .` scatters its scaffold across the root of the adopter's repository: `bundle.json`, `policy.json`, `realms.json`, `adapters/`, `agents/`, `scripts/`, `dialects/` (in spec-driven repositories) and `.forge/.gitignore`. Three of those names (`scripts/`, `agents/`, `policy.json`) collide with names a project commonly owns. The runtime state's `.forge/` predates the Brokkr name (decision 0019), so a new user sees two names for one tool. The current inventory is in `docs/guides/quickstart.md`'s Step 2.

## Operator ruling, 2026-10-11 (option A)

**Everything Brokkr writes into an adopter's repository lives in one hidden folder, `.brokkr/`**, like `.github/`:

- the tracked scaffold: `.brokkr/bundle.json`, `.brokkr/policy.json`, `.brokkr/realms.json`, `.brokkr/adapters/`, `.brokkr/agents/`, `.brokkr/scripts/` and `.brokkr/dialects/`;
- the runtime state in `.brokkr/state/`: the journal, results, ledger and `secrets.env`, kept out of git by `.brokkr/.gitignore`.

The legacy `.forge/` name retires for adopters. Brokkr's own repository is a recipe library, not an adopter scaffold, so its `recipes/`, `agents/` and `adapters/` stay where they are.

## Asked

1. **Discovery.** `brokkr` finds `.brokkr/` at the repository root, by walking up from the working directory to the git root. `brokkr run --feature "…"` then works without `--bundle`, `--realms` or `--db`. Explicit flags still win. State the precedence.
2. **Defaults.** `DEFAULT_DB`, the secrets default, `DEFAULT_AGENTS_DIR`, `DEFAULT_ADAPTERS_DIR` and the realms map's default path read the discovered folder. A bundle's script paths stay relative to the bundle.
3. **Old layouts.** A repository with the root layout, or an existing `.forge/` journal, is detected and refused with the exact `git mv` commands (or `brokkr init --migrate`), never half-read. A journal's history is never lost: say how an existing `.forge/forge.db` moves, or is read in place for one release.
4. **`init` and doctor.** `init` writes the folder and prints what it wrote. `brokkr doctor` reports the discovered folder, or its absence.
5. **Docs and tests.** The quickstart, `docs/guides/starters/`, the doc-truth paths and the init tests follow.
6. Relates to #432 (personal vs tracked configuration): the design says what of #432 it absorbs.

Design first: a decision recording the ruling and its details, then the build. The build changes CLI defaults in `cli_args.rs`, so it follows the other session's U6c8 (#625).

instructions.analyze:
# OpenSpec analyze

Judge duplication, ambiguity, underspecification, house alignment, coverage gaps, and inconsistency across proposal, deltas, design and tasks. Treat the realm house as the constitution. Return each finding with severity and its earliest owning artifact; zero findings is consistent.
instructions.clarify:
# OpenSpec clarify

Judge underspecified areas, unquantified language, missing decisions, capability/delta mismatches, and requirements without adequate scenarios. Return every ambiguity with the evidence needed to settle it; zero findings is clear.
instructions.design:
# OpenSpec design

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/design.md`. Record context, goals and non-goals, decisions with alternatives, risks, migration, and open questions. On return, revise the design and dependent artifacts so no finding is merely acknowledged.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.
instructions.implement:
# OpenSpec tasks

Write `openspec/changes/<change>/tasks.md` as numbered groups of checkboxes. Name the requirement served by every task. On return, repair the breakdown and its requirement coverage before implementation resumes.

# OpenSpec return

Revise the returned change in dependency order. Encode an answered ambiguity as a scenario, record design choices under `## Decisions`, and keep every dependent artifact coherent. Record a reasoned refusal in the owning artifact.

Change location: `openspec/changes/{change}`. Archive operation: ["openspec","archive","{change}","--yes"].

# OpenSpec archive

Folding a change is the last task: run the archive operation named above,
which moves the change directory under `openspec/changes/archive/` and
folds its deltas into `openspec/specs/`. Folding also records which change
wrote which capability, so every capability the change touched carries a
`## Provenance` list.

After the archive operation, open each capability's
`openspec/specs/<capability>/spec.md` that the change touched and append
exactly one line under a `## Provenance` heading held at the end of the
file:

`- \`<archived-directory-name>\` — folded <YYYY-MM-DD>`

`<archived-directory-name>` is the directory the archive operation
created under `openspec/changes/archive/`; `<YYYY-MM-DD>` is the day it
was folded. Append only: never rewrite, reorder or remove an existing
provenance line, because standing truth accumulates and is not edited into
a different meaning. The line is a pointer, not a summary — it names the
change and nothing else, and the why stays in the change directory.

house.content:
This realm is a Rust workspace. Production code is Rust under `crates/`; the
Rust-only architecture is recorded by decision 0009. Semantic changes carry a
decision document with status `proposed` because only the operator accepts one.
Intake seats read `README.md` and decisions 0004 and 0005 before framing a
commission, along with the code and history it touches.

The frozen v1 contracts under `contracts/`, the production table at
`policy/phase-machine.json`, and `reference/` (its schemas included) are
read-only.
A contract change lands as a new version file beside the old one, never as an
edit. The evaluator corpus under `fixtures/` is also frozen and is never
regenerated, only versioned.

Tests are part of every change. Extend the suite that proves the code, run
`cargo test --workspace`, compile `recipes/self`, and leave formatting, clippy,
and the exact-coverage gate clean before reporting success.

Commit completed work with `git` using the repository's message style. Never
push.

The supported hosts are Linux and macOS (decision 0063); WSL2 is Linux. Write
no Windows-conditional code, test or evidence.

## Architecture

Decision 0071 rules how code here is shaped. Build to it, and cite its ruling
numbers in what you judge. Where a gate named below holds a rule, the gate is
the authority, and a finding it would catch is the gate's.

- **Pure core (ruling 1).** `brokkr-core` and `brokkr-view` do no I/O and read
  no clock, environment or randomness. They run no process. Pass `now`, paths
  and environment in as arguments. Effects live in the crates above core and
  view, and are journaled.
- **Enums and data, not traits (ruling 2).** A closed set is an enum matched
  exhaustively, with no wildcard arm that decides behaviour. Anything an
  operator extends is data under `adapters/`, `agents/`, `recipes/` or
  `realms.json`, validated and digested. Add a trait only for a seam whose
  contract spans several operations that must stay consistent with one
  another, reached across a process or service boundary, and name that seam
  in its doc comment. `ProducerTransport` is the one such trait today. A test
  double alone does not make a seam: a single substitutable function is a
  closure seam (`*_with`, `*_in`), which is how the house inverts a
  dependency otherwise.
- **Typed at the edge (ruling 3).** Parse wire, file and harness data once
  into a type, with `serde` and `deny_unknown_fields` where the contract is
  closed. `serde_json::Value` never goes past the edge, into state, or back
  out by string key. Never put `format!("{:?}")` in anything digested or
  journaled. A doubly-optional field or a string vocabulary is a missing enum.
- **Small functions (ruling 4).** New and changed functions stay within 100
  lines, nesting depth 5 and 7 parameters. Cyclomatic complexity follows
  the operator's 2026-09-26 ruling: a function may reach the higher of 15
  and its baseline, so a new function stays within 15, an existing one may
  change freely up to 15, and one already over 15 may only shrink.
  Production files stay within 800 lines and test files within 2,000, and a
  file already over may not grow. Add no new `jscpd` clone in production
  code, test code or data. `quality/` holds the measured baseline. Today's
  offenders carry `#[allow(clippy::…)]`, and #337 converts them to
  `#[expect(clippy::…, reason = "…")]`. Add a suppression only by a ruling,
  and remove it when you fix the function. A new suppression is
  `#[expect(…, reason)]`, never `#[allow]`.
- **Once (ruling 5).** Every fact has one home. A repeated vocabulary, skeleton
  or helper becomes one function or one table. An agent is defined once under
  `agents/`, and seats hire it by reference. A recipe that differs from another
  by a model, a seat or an entry is an `extends` overlay, never a copy. The
  agent library does not yet accept `extends`, and #360 builds it. Until then,
  a variation of an agent lives at the seat that hires it, overridden in a
  recipe overlay. It is never a second agent file that restates the first. A
  copy that must exist, such as a script a bundle pins, is held to its source
  by a test.
- **Nothing unused (ruling 6).** Add no alias, agent, contract version, flag or
  `pub` item without a consumer, and prefer `pub(crate)`. A deprecation names
  the release that removes it.
- **One derivation (ruling 7).** A fact shown on two surfaces is derived once
  in `brokkr-view`. The CLI, the TUI and `ui.html` only paint it. The engine
  never admits anything by a display-crate function.
- **Typed errors (ruling 8).** Return a `thiserror` enum whose `Display` keeps
  the operator's text. Tests match variants and pin each module's text once.
  Add no new `Result<_, String>`.
- **Tests that bind (ruling 9).** Assert exact values or variants, never
  `is_err()` alone. Show that every new test binds: a compiling mutation that
  removes the behaviour must make it fail. Restore the behaviour and record
  the failing test. Share fixtures through builders. Never change the process
  environment without a guard that restores it on unwind. A production guard
  left out because the exact-coverage gate would count it unreachable carries
  a removal-control test for the invariant that makes it unreachable, and the
  comment explaining the omission names that test.
- **The house's patterns (ruling 10).**
  - A harness is a module behind `AdapterKind`. This is the target form;
    today all five kinds share one module, and #347 and #348 build the
    split.
  - A CLI verb is a `Cmd` variant plus a handler.
  - A long parameter list becomes a parameter object.
  - Argv and mount tables are built with a builder.
  - Observing the world is split from deciding on it.
  - Never use a trait-object registry for a closed set.

Judges rate a finding against these rulings by this table, and cite the ruling
number:

- **info:** something a house gate would catch. The gate's verdict is the
  authority.
- **low:** a new or changed function over a ceiling, a rule written a second
  time, an item added without a consumer, or a `Value` carried past its edge
  within one module.
- **medium:** an untyped vocabulary that crosses crates, recipe or agent data
  copied instead of extended, a fact derived a second time on another surface,
  an error matched by its text, or a new test that cannot fail.
- **high or above:** any violation that hides a fail-open path or weakens a
  refusal. It is carried as a security finding.

A principle the implementer bent knowingly, and named with its reason in
`notes`, is still rated, and the judge carries that reason with the finding.

## Release configuration

The release manager prepares the candidate and profile patches; the operator
publishes them. Local validation is preparation work. Remote CI on the final PR
head, publication, channel updates and live-profile verification are handoff
steps, recorded as pending until their remote results exist. Historical
"live from" channel versions and old journal examples are historical facts,
not current-version references to replace.

result.notes:
Built the operator's ruling of 2026-10-14 (option 1) as one commit, ff0ec09b, on top of 6d46af6a. No rebase, squash or amend.

RULE. state_moves now decides no_link(root/.forge) first, before Forge::at and before any git question. no_link walks .forge and every entry under it with places::entry (symlink_metadata) and never follows a link. A .forge that is a link, or any link at any depth under it, refuses as the new FolderError::Link { path }, naming the min path in component order, which is the first in sorted walk order. Its text is the ruling's verbatim. An unreadable entry or directory refuses as Unreadable. Old-layout detection (places.rs) is unchanged: a linked .forge is still StateOnly/Root, and only the move list refuses.

DELETED as unreachable:
- links.rs (the whole file; the walk lives in folder.rs);
- FolderError::ForgeHoldsRoot, LinkedTracked and Link(LinkRefusal);
- tracked::Index, including itself (held now returns Vec<Vec<u8>>);
- tracked()'s forge parameter;
- Forge::Link and Forge::linked;
- Move::Unlink, with its '# .forge is a link' line and 'rm .forge';
- the ignore-file link case (ignore_stands now takes is_file only).
Their pinned texts and tests went too:
- folder_tests: a_linked_forge_whose_entries_git_tracks_refuses, and a_link_the_moves_would_strand_refuses (its unreadable-subdirectory half moved into a_forge_that_cannot_be_listed_refuses);
- brokkr_folder: a_linked_forge_is_removed_as_a_link, plus the stranding_refusals, linked_refusals, escaping, holds_root, linked_tracked, commit_link and links() helpers, and Shape.linked.
Kept: Sparse, Uncommitted (including the row for a .forge committed as a link and then made a directory, now built in its own `then`), TrackedSubmodule, Unwatched, Untracked, NotUtf8, ControlCharacter, IgnoreNotAFile (text unchanged), HalfMoved, Root, StateOnly, MapSource::now, folder_bundle and places.rs.

TESTS.
- the_listed_moves_empty_every_forge keeps executing every arm of enum Move. builder_arms still reads it, and Unlink is gone from both the enum and arm_of.
- It has four link refusal rows: .forge itself (a link to a directory holding entries git tracks, so the rule is shown to precede git), .forge/.gitignore, .forge/forge.db, and .forge/results/run/out. Each asserts the exact stderr, that files() is unchanged, and that .brokkr does not exist.
- a_linked_entry_is_the_entry (a 0083-named test) now asserts the link refusal for a linked .forge, plus the untouched journal; its bundle.json-link half is unchanged.
- New unit test the_first_link_in_sorted_walk_order_is_named.
- an_ignore_entry_that_is_not_a_file_or_a_link_refuses: its link half now matches FolderError::Link.

REMOVAL CONTROLS (each planted, run, failed, restored):
1. Nested walk skipped (`found.is_dir() && path == forge`): brokkr_folder::the_listed_moves_empty_every_forge failed at row 'Link'. The nested row printed the state-only list ('mv .forge/results .brokkr/state/results' ...) where the refusal of .forge/results/run/out was expected.
2. .forge itself exempt (`found.is_symlink() && path != forge`): a_linked_entry_is_the_entry and the property test failed with '<root>/.forge is a file, not Brokkr's state directory: move it aside'.
3. Ignore file exempt (`&& !path.ends_with(IGNORE)`): the property test failed with '.forge/.gitignore is neither a file nor a link ...', and an_ignore_entry_that_is_not_a_file_or_a_link_refuses failed its Link match.
4. `.next()` for `.min()`: the_first_link_in_sorted_walk_order_is_named failed, naming .forge/z. Its first version passed this control, because tmpfs lists the newest entry first. I rebuilt it so the sorted-first link is created between the others, and then it bit.

GATES, all run in this session:
- cargo fmt --check: clean.
- cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --all-features --locked -D warnings: clean, no unfulfilled #[expect], suppressions unchanged.
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --lib: 782 passed, 1 ignored.
- cargo test -p brokkr-cli --test it (suppressions:: included): 632 passed, 3 ignored.
- --bins and --doc: 0 tests.
- typos --hidden, git diff --check, quality/ratchet.sh files ('file size holds'), clones ('duplication holds') and api ('public API holds'): all clean.
- compile --bundle recipes/self: OK.
Only brokkr-cli was touched. The exact-coverage gate is the controller's and was not run, so it is pending.

LINE COUNTS before -> after:
- folder.rs 686 -> 665
- links.rs 164 -> deleted
- tracked.rs 273 -> 251
- folder_tests.rs 720 -> 656
- tests/brokkr_folder.rs 1749 -> 1546
No jscpd or suppression baseline names these files (grep of quality/), so no baseline shrinks. Public API unchanged. docs/reference/cli.md unchanged (no help text moved).

DOCS. Every doc comment that described link moves or resolution was rewritten: state_moves, ignore_stands, Forge, forge_entries, IgnoreNotAFile, ForgeNotADirectory, tracked and held. A git grep for the deleted names and the 'rm removes the link' text finds nothing. Decision 0083 was not edited.

FOR THE OPERATOR'S ADDENDUM, 0083 sentences this ruling narrows:
- Ruling 4's 'Every entry is read by its own entry, never through a link: `.brokkr`, `bundle.json` and `.forge` are each judged by what stands at that name, so a symbolic link there is the entry, whatever it names.' This still holds for detection, but the move list no longer treats a linked .forge as an entry to empty and rm.
- The tests list's `a_linked_entry_is_the_entry (a `.forge` that is a symbolic link to a directory holding a journal, with no root `bundle.json`, gives the state-only text, ...)`. It now gives the one link refusal.

ASSUMPTIONS AND NOTES.
- The Link text displays the path unescaped. A link whose name holds a control character is named raw, not escaped as ControlCharacter is. That is an exotic LOW residual under the 2026-09-26 threat model.
- IgnoreNotAFile keeps its pinned text ('neither a file nor a link'), which a non-link entry still satisfies.
- Move::lines still returns a Vec although every arm is now one line. I left it, per 'delete what the rule makes unreachable, and no more'. Possible follow-up.
